constraints: Fabric-only: Spark/SJDs, Fabric Environment, Lakehouse/OneLake, Fabric-native orchestration/observability only
No external worker services, Azure ML, Container Apps, AKS, Functions, VMs, or non-Fabric compute
Do not modify production pipelines/notebooks, legacy pointers/views/gold, Reflex, semantic models/reports, production authorization
No runtime model/dependency downloads; offline export/localization only
CPU-only wheel publication; reject CUDA/NVIDIA/ROCm dependency markers

items.title: No checked-in SJD main program
items.recommendation: Add a small driver entry point and top-level executor callable; move deployment settings to a validated config object and Fabric Environment.
items.correctness_guardrail: SJD entry points parse and validate args before touching Spark state; import-time failures fail closed.
items.evidence: people_counter.fabric_candidate_a_jobs.control_main/process_main/gold_main and people_counter.fabric_benchmark_jobs.control_main/process_main/gold_main are already checked-in, wheel-installed, top-level argparse entry points consumed by SJD definitions built in fabric_candidate_a.py/fabric_benchmark_jobs.py (build_sjd_v2_definition). Live-proven per verified baseline (benchmark namespace clean/terminal, 11 SUCCEEDED jobs).

items.title: Unsafe production memory scaling (per-executor memory x executor count)
items.recommendation: Use the minimum usable executor memory and a placement-independent cap, or enforce a placement strategy that proves the stronger bound.
items.correctness_guardrail: compute_memory_cap uses min(executor.max_memory_bytes) across the live inventory, never a per-executor-then-multiplied assumption; fails closed if measured peak RSS does not fit.
items.evidence: New module people_counter/fabric_executor_inventory.py implements compute_memory_cap(executors, headroom, peak_rss_bytes) using min() across live executors (placement-independent cap), wired into sjd_process.build_profile_from_inventory and now into fabric_benchmark_jobs._benchmark_execution_profile (this session).

items.title: Hash repartition instead of explicit bucket-to-physical-partition mapping

items.correctness_guardrail: execute_sjd_bucket_partition asserts the Spark TaskContext physical partition id equals the planned bucket's explicit mapping before processing, failing closed on mismatch.
items.evidence: people_counter/sjd_process.py execute_sjd_bucket_partition (and _task_identity) already assert TaskContext.partitionId() against the planned bucket id; this is pre-existing, previously live-validated machinery per the verified baseline's zero-findings benchmark runs.

items.title: Incomplete retry isolation (task-attempt identity, _SUCCESS-last sealing)

items.title: Claim defaults eliminate model-load amortization (claim size defaults to one video)
items.recommendation: Keep one video for canary only; use a measured bounded batch for benchmark and production.
items.correctness_guardrail: plan_duration_lpt(minimum_videos_per_group=...) fails closed (ProcessValidationError) when the claimed workload could have filled every bucket to the minimum but did not, preventing silent amortization loss.
items.evidence: people_counter/fabric_executor_inventory.py assert_minimum_videos_per_group (new) wired into people_counter/sjd_process.py plan_duration_lpt via the new minimum_videos_per_group parameter (this session); tests test_lpt_accepts_a_workload_that_meets_the_minimum_videos_per_group and test_lpt_fails_closed_when_a_group_falls_short_of_the_minimum in tests/test_sjd_process.py. RUBBER-DUCK-VERIFIED DOWNGRADE: the live entry point sjd_process.run_process_batch (called from fabric_candidate_a_jobs.process_main) never passes minimum_videos_per_group to plan_duration_lpt, so this guard is exercised only by direct unit tests, never by the live claim-size-defaults-to-one-video path the original gap was about; downgraded from implemented to partial. See plan5-minimum-videos-per-runtime-group for the identical finding.

items.title: No accepted six-hour Candidate A capacity result
items.recommendation: Persist reproducible benchmark evidence and run the full acceptance gate before production sizing.
items.correctness_guardrail: The six-hour gate requires the one-sided 95% LCB of aggregate throughput to reach 416.67x with zero correctness/memory/queue/publication failures before being run at all.
items.evidence: Six-hour gate machinery (calculate_statistics, moving_block_bootstrap_lcb, select_block_length, evaluate_reliability_gates) already exists and is live-proven per the verified baseline. The gate correctly has NOT been run: best measured aggregate throughput is 1.5899x against a 416.67x requirement (262.07x short); the document's own Executive Summary concludes 'a sustained test cannot rescue a candidate that misses the throughput gate by this magnitude.' This item's six-hour run remains intentionally not executed in this engagement for the same documented reason.

items.section: 1. Convert the worker to an SJD
items.title: One nonempty claim starts exactly one bounded Spark application
items.recommendation: Do not create one SJD per video or a pipeline ForEach.
items.correctness_guardrail: run_process_batch takes one batch_id and plans/executes all claimed items within that one Spark application; no per-video job submission path exists.
items.evidence: people_counter/sjd_process.py run_process_batch and fabric_candidate_a_jobs.process_main/fabric_benchmark_jobs.process_main operate on one --batch-id per invocation, consistent with the one-claim-one-application invariant.

items.section: 2. Make the scheduler physically match the plan
items.title: Inventory active executors after resources are ready
items.recommendation: Inventory active executors after resources are ready (step 1 of the benchmark algorithm).
items.correctness_guardrail: discover_active_executors polls the live Spark AppStatusStore (SparkContext.statusStore().executorList(True) via Py4J) until executor identity/cores/memory are stable for stability_polls consecutive polls and meet minimum_executors, else fails closed with ExecutorInventoryError.
items.evidence: New module people_counter/fabric_executor_inventory.py (prior session in this engagement), tests in tests/test_fabric_executor_inventory.py. Wired this session into fabric_benchmark_jobs._benchmark_execution_profile and a new resource-inventory CLI action, replacing the prior hard-coded 'exactly five executors' assertion. THREE live-Fabric-discovered correctness bugs were found and fixed via actual job runs against the deployed Spark 4.1.1 runtime (benchmark namespace, item 547a4aa8-1927-4597-9f22-d153c5976d2b), not merely unit tests: (1) SparkContext.statusTracker().getExecutorInfos() does not exist on the deployed runtime (py4j.protocol.Py4JError: Method getExecutorInfos([]) does not exist); fixed by calling SparkContext.statusStore().executorList(activeOnly=True) directly via Py4J and draining its Java iterator. (2) hasattr(java_object, name) is always true for any name on a live Py4J JVM proxy (Py4J lazily builds a callable proxy per attribute access and only discovers a missing JVM method on invocation), so the hasattr-based field fallback never actually fell through to the next candidate name; live-verified failure: py4j.protocol.Py4JError: Method host([]) does not exist (the real ExecutorSummary only exposes hostPort()). Fixed by having _field attempt each candidate invocation and catch py4j.protocol.Py4JError (optional import) to fall through, rather than probing with hasattr. (3) A newly-registering executor can transiently report maxMemory=0 before its BlockManager finishes registering; live-verified failure: ExecutorInventoryError: executor '5' reports non-positive max memory, which previously propagated uncaught out of the polling loop and crashed the whole job instead of being retried. Fixed by catching ExecutorInventoryError per-poll inside discover_active_executors, treating it as 'not yet stable' (reset stability state, keep polling), and only failing closed -- with the most recent validation error chained via `raise ... from last_error` for diagnosability -- if the deadline elapses without ever observing a valid, stable inventory. All three fixes verified live: job instance bbab729d-3b73-495a-ac62-6ccc7d1490e5 (wheel 0.9.14, pre-fix-3) reproduced bug 3; Fix 3 verified live in a fourth run on wheel 0.9.15 (job instance 131f15c1-9a8a-4e4d-a166-0fdd16bed1b0, Spark app application_1791322220738_0001): Final app status: SUCCEEDED, exitCode: 0; resource-inventory JSON report confirms 5 live executors discovered (executor_id 1-5, host vm-a1f87619/vm-c2c82015/vm-77f39536/vm-a0792670/vm-21c74928, total_cores=8 each, max_memory_bytes=35888981606 each [~33.4 GiB, matching the BlockManager registration logs]), task_cpus=1, slots=40, planned_task_count=40. Each fix is covered by dedicated regression tests using the real py4j.protocol.Py4JError class (not a plain mock), 100% line+branch coverage, and focused mutmut runs with zero non-equivalent survivors.

items.section: 2. Make the scheduler physically match the plan
items.title: Compute CPU slots per executor: S = sum floor(C_i / T)
items.recommendation: Compute CPU slots per executor from observed executor cores and spark.task.cpus.
items.correctness_guardrail: compute_slots sums floor(total_cores / task_cpus) over the live executor list; rejects non-positive task_cpus and empty executor lists.
items.evidence: people_counter/fabric_executor_inventory.py compute_slots implements S = sum(floor(C_i/T)) exactly as specified. RUBBER-DUCK FINDING RESOLVED: this coarse global sum is no longer the sole concurrency bound -- plan_task_width also calls assert_executor_placement_safe, which fails closed unless EVERY individual executor's own floor(cores/task_cpus) ceiling fits its own measured memory (not merely the inventory-wide minimum), directly closing the 'Spark can colocate every task on the biggest executor' gap the rubber-duck review identified.

items.section: 2. Make the scheduler physically match the plan
items.title: Compute conservative memory cap M from measured worker high-water RSS
items.recommendation: M = floor(U_min * (1-H) / R_peak).
items.correctness_guardrail: Uses min() usable memory across executors and measured peak_rss_bytes; fails closed if the measured RSS does not fit the minimum usable memory at all.
items.evidence: people_counter/fabric_executor_inventory.py compute_memory_cap; peak_rss_bytes is sourced from the new fabric_capability_probe.probe_rss_high_water_mark() capability probe (this session) rather than assumed. RUBBER-DUCK FINDING RESOLVED ('Memory planning is neither placement-safe nor active'): compute_memory_cap's inventory-wide minimum is deliberately only a coarse global ceiling; the actual placement-safety guarantee comes from the companion function per_executor_memory_slots/assert_executor_placement_safe (also in fabric_executor_inventory.py), which computes each executor's OWN min(floor(cores/task_cpus), floor(usable_memory/peak_rss_bytes)) and fails closed if any executor's cores-based ceiling would exceed its own measured-safe memory concurrency -- this is wired into the live call path via plan_task_width -> sjd_process.build_profile_from_inventory -> fabric_candidate_a_jobs._fabric_process_profile -> process_main, and into fabric_capability_probe.probe_executor_peak_rss_bytes (executor-side RSS measurement, not driver-side), closing the 'Candidate RSS probe is driver-side' finding as well.

items.section: 2. Make the scheduler physically match the plan
items.title: P = min(N, S, M, P_operator)
items.recommendation: Compute a deterministic, placement-safe task count as the minimum of all limits.
items.correctness_guardrail: plan_task_width computes min(slots, memory_cap, operator_cap) and fails closed if the result collapses to zero.
items.evidence: people_counter/fabric_executor_inventory.py plan_task_width / TaskWidthPlacement. RUBBER-DUCK FINDING RESOLVED ('Executor discovery contradicts the execution profile'): execute_sjd_partition (sjd_process.py) no longer rejects anything other than one executor core/one task CPU -- it validates task_cpus against REVIEWED_TASK_CPU_WIDTHS = frozenset({1, 2, 4}) and only requires task_cpus <= executor_cores, preserving the reviewed 1/2/4 widths while removing the prior one-core-only rejection. Physical partitions are planned from TaskWidthPlacement.planned_task_count (the summed per-executor placement-safe slot count), not bare executor count, per build_profile_from_inventory's docstring and implementation.

items.section: 2. Make the scheduler physically match the plan
items.title: Map bucket_id % P explicitly to the physical partition and assert on the executor
items.recommendation: Map bucket_id % P explicitly to the physical partition in each wave and assert the mapping on the executor.
items.correctness_guardrail: Executor-side assertion compares the Spark-reported physical partition id against the planned bucket-to-partition mapping; mismatch raises and aborts the task rather than silently processing the wrong bucket.
items.evidence: Pre-existing in people_counter/sjd_process.py (BucketPlan/WavePlan/execute_sjd_bucket_partition); live-proven per verified baseline.

items.section: 2. Make the scheduler physically match the plan
items.title: Predicted-seconds cost model with visible fallback to duration
items.recommendation: predicted_seconds formula trained/calibrated from completed attempts, falling back visibly to duration when a feature or model version is unknown.
items.correctness_guardrail: Predictor must be versioned/auditable and must fall back to duration-based LPT when insufficient telemetry exists; never silently guesses.
items.evidence: Cold-start duration-only LPT exists and is live-proven (people_counter/sjd_process.py plan_duration_lpt). The calibrated multi-feature predicted_seconds regression (codec/resolution/density/cold-load coefficients) described in the document is NOT yet implemented; this session added the event-log ingest/task-overlap measurement (people_counter/fabric_spark_event_ingest.py) that would supply the telemetry such a predictor needs, but the predictor model itself, its versioning, and its promotion gate remain future work. Per the task's explicit instruction ('cold-start fallback remains duration LPT... Make prediction versioned and auditable'), the safe, already-gated fallback remains in force; no uncalibrated predictor has been substituted.

items.section: 2. Make the scheduler physically match the plan
items.title: Route long videos to a larger lease class; do not split without checkpoint semantics
items.recommendation: Long videos that cannot finish within the lease budget should be routed to a larger resource/lease class; do not split them until tracker-state checkpoint and transfer semantics have been validated.
items.correctness_guardrail: Admission must reject (not silently split) any single video whose predicted cost exceeds the configured lease budget.
items.evidence: people_counter/fabric_executor_production.py require_configured_lease_budget / require_live_wave_budget and sjd_process.admit_lease already fail closed rather than splitting a video across tasks; no tracker-state checkpoint/transfer mechanism exists or is implemented (correctly, since the document says not to split until that is validated).

items.title: Canary/Characterization/Approval/Production fixed-allocation profiles
items.recommendation: Use fixed allocation for approval; treat dynamic allocation as a later, separately gated experiment.
items.correctness_guardrail: ExecutionProfile.fixed_allocation is asserted True and spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled='false' is a reviewed, asserted Spark setting for the benchmark fixed profile.
items.evidence: people_counter/sjd_process.py ExecutionProfile(fixed_allocation=True) plus fabric_benchmark_jobs._benchmark_execution_profile asserting spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled=='false'. Note: fabric_candidate_a_jobs._fabric_process_profile (the non-benchmark Candidate A production-namespace profile) intentionally requires the *reviewed* dynamic live pool for that namespace -- an existing, separately reviewed decision this engagement did not alter, since it is outside the benchmark SJD wrapper scope this task is permitted to change.

items.section: 4. Coordinate task width and native inference threads
items.title: Set OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS/NUMEXPR thread env vars before importing/initializing the model stack
items.recommendation: Set OMP_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, and NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS before importing or initializing the model stack.
items.correctness_guardrail: configure_cpu_runtime sets all native thread environment variables prior to any torch/cv2 import in the calling process.
items.evidence: people_counter/cpu_runtime.py configure_cpu_runtime (pre-existing, live-proven per baseline).

items.section: 4. Coordinate task width and native inference threads
items.title: Runtime readback proving effective thread settings; fail on oversubscription
items.recommendation: Add runtime readback proving effective thread settings and fail on oversubscription beyond the reviewed profile.
items.correctness_guardrail: verify_effective_thread_settings reads torch.get_num_threads()/get_num_interop_threads(), cv2.getNumThreads(), the ONNX SessionOptions override, and all native env vars, raising ThreadOversubscriptionError if the live effective values exceed the reviewed budget.
items.evidence: people_counter/cpu_runtime.py EffectiveThreadSettings, ThreadOversubscriptionError, read_effective_thread_settings, verify_effective_thread_settings (implemented and verified this engagement, including a bug fix making _onnx_thread_override read from the correct environ source). tests/test_cpu_runtime.py: 18 tests + 12 subtests passing.

items.section: 4. Coordinate task width and native inference threads
items.title: Avoid a nested ThreadPoolExecutor inside Spark tasks
items.recommendation: Avoid a nested ThreadPoolExecutor; Spark already provides process-level parallelism, and sharing a mutable model across threads is unsafe for many model libraries.
items.correctness_guardrail: No ThreadPoolExecutor/threading usage exists inside the per-partition inference loop; the model runtime is used sequentially per video.
items.evidence: Verified by inspection: people_counter/pipelines/rtdetr_osnet.py and people_counter/fabric_executor_partition.py process videos strictly sequentially inside one partition with no nested thread pool.

items.title: Deterministic homogeneous grouping by runtime/model/config/format/resolution/FPS profile
items.recommendation: Increase the homogeneous claimed batch so every active partition normally receives several compatible videos.
items.correctness_guardrail: Grouping keys must be exact (runtime cache key, model, config, format, resolution, FPS); LPT bucket assignment is deterministic given identical inputs.
items.evidence: people_counter/fabric_executor_production.py plan_largest_cost_first and sjd_process.py plan_duration_lpt group by compatible profile keys; live-proven per the verified baseline's clean/terminal benchmark namespace runs.

items.title: Sequential multi-video processing per partition with fresh tracker/result state per video
items.recommendation: Run multiple videos sequentially inside each partition/runtime so one model load yields cache hits; fresh tracker/result state per video.
items.correctness_guardrail: Worker-global model-runtime reuse is performance-only (never a correctness dependency); every video must receive fresh tracker and result state even when detector weights are reused.
items.evidence: people_counter/fabric_executor_partition.py's runtime cache plus people_counter/pipelines/rtdetr_osnet.py constructing fresh tracker state per process_frame_batch call; live-proven per baseline.

items.title: Persist model_load_count, model_load_seconds, cache-key hash, and cache hits
items.recommendation: Persist model_load_count, model_load_seconds, cache-key hash, and cache hits.
items.correctness_guardrail: Telemetry fields must be recorded per attempt, never fabricated; a missing field must be recorded with an explicit null reason (fabric_capability_probe).
items.evidence: RUBBER-DUCK-VERIFIED DOWNGRADE: WorkAttemptTelemetry (people_counter/fabric_benchmark.py) has only logical_work_id/source_id/attempt_id/started_at/completed_at/status/committed/processed_frames/partial_output_visible/error_category -- no model_load_count, model_load_seconds, or cache_key_hash field exists anywhere on this dataclass; TelemetryStage.MODEL_CACHE is only a generic stage-name enum member, not a typed record of these values. people_counter/fabric_source_cache.py LocalizedSourceCache does expose hit/miss/eviction counters (now wired into the live path, see plan8-localized-content-hash-cache), but those counters are not yet persisted onto WorkAttemptTelemetry or any other per-attempt record. Required load duration and cache-key hash are genuinely missing from telemetry; downgraded from live_proven to partial.

items.title: Explicit minimum videos-per-runtime-group when workload permits
items.recommendation: Bounded videos per partition; explicit minimum videos-per-runtime group when workload permits.
items.correctness_guardrail: Fails closed (never silently under-fills a group) whenever the total claimed workload could have met the minimum for every group.
items.evidence: RUBBER-DUCK-VERIFIED DOWNGRADE: assert_minimum_videos_per_group exists and is unit-tested, and sjd_process.plan_duration_lpt accepts an optional minimum_videos_per_group kwarg that calls it when non-None. However, the live entry point sjd_process.run_process_batch (called from fabric_candidate_a_jobs.process_main) calls plan_duration_lpt(envelope.items, profile, peak_rss_bytes=peak_rss_bytes) with no minimum_videos_per_group argument at all, so the parameter defaults to None and the assertion is never evaluated in the live call path. The function is implemented and tested in isolation but dead in production; downgraded from implemented to partial.

items.section: 6. Increase detector batching before changing models
items.title: Test detector batch sizes 1, 2, 4 (8 only after RSS headroom)
items.recommendation: Test detector batch sizes 1, 2, and 4; test 8 only after RSS headroom is demonstrated.
items.correctness_guardrail: Promotion requires exact final unique-person/directed-line counts, matching sampled frame indices, and bounded detector-score differences near thresholds.
items.evidence: RUBBER-DUCK-VERIFIED DOWNGRADE: process_frame_batch forms frame batches and performs one detector call per batch (pre-existing baseline capability), but this engagement did not run or re-verify the specific promotion criteria from this item's own correctness_guardrail (exact matching unique-person/directed-line counts, matching sampled frame indices, bounded detector-score differences near thresholds) at batch widths 1, 2, and 4 specifically. The baseline language cited as evidence ('the implementation already forms frame batches...') describes capability, not a completed promotion test matrix; downgraded from live_proven to partial. RSS-headroom-gated batch-8 promotion remains a separately gated experiment not run in this engagement.

items.section: 7. Remove avoidable image copies and repeated work
items.title: Resize BGR before RGB conversion; defer full-resolution RGB until ReID needs it
items.recommendation: resize BGR to detector dimensions; convert the small detector image to RGB; perform detection; create a full-resolution RGB image only when surviving person candidates require ReID.
items.correctness_guardrail: cv2.resize(cv2.cvtColor(...)) and cv2.cvtColor(cv2.resize(...)) proven byte-identical via live cv2 experiment (np.array_equal, max diff 0) before promotion; exact tracking/counting outputs preserved.
items.evidence: people_counter/pipelines/rtdetr_osnet.py predict_detector_results/extract_person_detections/process_frame/process_frame_batch refactored this engagement to resize-before-convert and defer full-resolution RGB conversion until NMS determines surviving candidates exist. tests/test_association.py (3 tests incl. a new zero-candidate-skips-embedder test) and tests/test_pipeline_components.py (3 call-site updates) all passing; full suite regression-free (1319 passed, 2 skipped).

items.section: 8. Reduce storage and Spark action overhead
items.title: Hash bytes while copying source into attempt-local staging
items.recommendation: Hash bytes while copying the source into attempt-local staging instead of copying and then rereading the entire staged file for SHA-256.
items.correctness_guardrail: Digest must be computed over the exact bytes written in the same pass (no behavior change to the resulting hash value, verified by pre-existing tests that assert specific hash values); never a whole-file read()/read_bytes().
items.evidence: UPDATED (P1-D InputResolver work, this engagement): the live Candidate A dispatch path (fabric_candidate_a_jobs.process_main -> _localize_process_inputs -> local_spark._verified_video/_localized_models_dir) now calls people_counter.fabric_input_resolver.stream_sha256 directly with a bounded _CHUNK_BYTES read loop -- confirmed by test_stream_sha256_reads_in_bounded_chunks_never_the_whole_file (instruments Path.open to assert every read uses the bounded chunk size, never None/whole-file) and by local_spark.py:_verified_video/_localized_models_dir, which hash the resolved/copied file incrementally instead of shutil.copyfile + reread. people_counter/fabric_executor_production.py staged_executor_source (the function this item previously cited) remains unused dead code with zero production callers outside its own test file; the live requirement is now met through the resolver module instead, so implementation_symbol has been corrected to point at the code the live path actually calls. Focused mutmut: fabric_input_resolver.py 113/113 mutants killed, local_spark.py _verified_video/_localized_models_dir 153/153 mutants killed.

items.section: 8. Reduce storage and Spark action overhead
items.title: Avoid DISK_ONLY + count() followed by another scan for the Delta write
items.recommendation: Make the Delta append the materializing action and collect counts from partition metrics or the committed snapshot.
items.correctness_guardrail: Counts must come from the bounded per-partition staging receipt (record_count) or the committed Delta snapshot, never from a second full re-scan of the data.
items.evidence: people_counter/sjd_process.py PartitionStagingReceipt.record_count is produced by the same pass that stages records (stage_partition_records); StreamingSparkExecutionHarness collects only receipts via one Spark action and reconstructs full rows by reading already-staged files directly, avoiding a second DISK_ONLY+count()+rescan pattern. 13 new tests in tests/test_sjd_process.py.

items.section: 8. Reduce storage and Spark action overhead
items.title: Avoid per-video take(1)/count() calls when the driver already has publication lists
items.recommendation: Avoid per-video take(1) and later count() calls when the driver already has the publication lists and their lengths.
items.correctness_guardrail: Validation must use len() on driver-held in-memory lists rather than issuing additional Spark actions against the same data.
items.evidence: Verified by inspection: people_counter/sjd_process.py validate_staged_records and fabric_candidate_a_control.py operate on driver-held Python lists/dicts already materialized from one Spark action; no additional per-video take(1)/count() action pattern exists in the current implementation.

items.section: 8. Reduce storage and Spark action overhead
items.title: Filter line-count objects before converting every sampled-frame record
items.recommendation: Production should retain crossing changes plus the final cumulative record, rather than one row for every sampled frame.
items.correctness_guardrail: Only rows where line counts changed plus the final cumulative row are retained; typed schema, not an unfiltered per-frame JSON blob.
items.evidence: people_counter/sjd_process.py sparse_line_records already implements change-detection filtering plus retains the final record; pre-existing and live-proven per baseline.

items.section: 8. Reduce storage and Spark action overhead
items.title: Yield partition results incrementally instead of retaining a complete partition in memory; avoid full driver collect
items.recommendation: Yield partition results incrementally rather than retaining a complete partition's records in Python memory. Stream/write partition results incrementally to immutable attempt staging and return only bounded summaries/task receipts to driver.
items.correctness_guardrail: The driver-bound mapPartitions output must be a single bounded receipt object (content hash, record count, work ids), never the full row list; full rows travel executor->disk directly and are reconstructed by the driver reading staged files, never via Spark RDD-to-driver collection of full rows.
items.evidence: New this engagement: people_counter/sjd_process.py PartitionStagingReceipt, stage_partition_records, read_staged_partition_records, execute_sjd_bucket_partition_streaming, StreamingSparkExecutionHarness (additive alongside the existing SparkExecutionHarness, same list[dict] external contract). 13 new tests added to tests/test_sjd_process.py covering staging idempotency/conflict, read-back round-trip, and fail-closed receipt verification.

items.section: 8. Reduce storage and Spark action overhead
items.title: Localized executor cache keyed by content hash with bounded eviction and hit/miss metrics

items.evidence: FABRIC_PLATFORM_BLOCKED (this engagement, after wheel 0.9.20 went live): the staged live matrix could not be completed because Spark job starts against Environment 3e580f48-9ff7-4bc6-af2e-a59158029ada / capacity 27fe2dc5-cdfd-4a28-8bba-75413296d02d (F64) began failing with errorCode=Spark_User_AutoClassification_AttemptDiagnostics, message='Job failed during run time with state=[dead]' (e.g. jobInstanceId 82dbbf21-dfe4-4289-b6a0-3faa8750b849, runningDuration ~145-180s) for BOTH the modified process SJD and the UNCHANGED control SJD's resource-inventory action (code untouched this engagement, historically ~67% success rate per /sparkJobDefinitions/{item}/livySessions: 31/46 Succeeded over the prior several hours). A fake/non-existent batch id crashed identically to real batches, ruling out batch-content dependence. Decisive platform-side evidence: fetching the failed job's own driver logs via GET /v1/workspaces/{ws}/sparkJobDefinitions/{item}/livySessions/{livyId}/applications/{sparkApplicationId}/logs (type=driver) returned HTTP 404 'unknown app: application_1791352791802_0001' -- the Spark application that Fabric's own Livy session record assigned never registered with the log/history backend at all -- while the IDENTICAL endpoint returned HTTP 200 with full stdout/stderr for a prior Succeeded session's application id (application_1791348417073_0001) moments later, proving the fetch mechanism and credentials are correct and the gap is server-side. The F64 capacity object itself reports state=Active (GET /v1/capacities), ruling out administrative pause; a web search found no public Azure/Fabric service-health incident for the relevant window. Five consecutive resource-inventory retries spanning ~35 minutes (05:28, 05:37, 05:50, 05:58, 06:05 UTC) all failed identically, versus the historical ~67% baseline success rate, indicating an active (likely transient) platform-side Spark session/container provisioning degradation on this capacity/environment rather than a regression introduced by any code change in this engagement. Per task instructions this is recorded as FABRIC_PLATFORM_BLOCKED with exact evidence rather than mislabeled as inapplicable or silently left partial; STEP 1-7 code/tests/wheel/publish work is complete and independent of this blocker. See the final RETURN summary for the complete timeline and all job/session/application IDs.
